blocks.text: 119 Musaph for the New Year 119

Holy Ark in awe to soften anger and wrath; Thy people surround them like a wall and Thou dost watch from heaven to show them mercy. They lift up their eyes to Thee in heaven, they pour out their hearts before Thee like water and Thou dost hear them from heaven, lest they stumble with their tongue, be confused in their repetition or be shamed in their confidence, lest their congregation be disgraced by them and their mouth say aught that is not according to Thy will. For those favoured by Thee, O Lord our God, are indeed favoured and those who are pitied by Thee are truly pitied, as we know well, O Lord our God, that he whom Thou dost favour is favoured and he whom Thou hast pitied, is pitied. As it is written in Thy Torah: ‘I will favour him whom I favour and pity him whom I pity’.
uncertainties: 'dis-graced' is broken across a line; I treated it as a line-break hyphen only.

blocks.text: ונאמר And it was said: ‘Let those who trust in Thee, O Lord God of Hosts, not be shamed through me, let those who seek Thee, O God of Israel, not be disgraced through me’.
uncertainties: The rubric (בפפד״מ…) and the ark open/close instructions are not translated on the English page.

blocks.text: אוחילה I pray to God, I entreat His countenance, I beg Him for pleasant speech. In the assembly of people I sing to His might, I utter exultations because of His deeds. Reflections of the heart belong to man but pleasant speech is from the Lord. O Lord, open my lips that my mouth may proclaim Thy fame. Let the words of my mouth find favour and the meditation of my heart before Thee, O Lord, my rock and my redeemer.
uncertainties: There is a small dot below 'my redeemer.', probably a blemish.

blocks.text: על כן Therefore we hope for Thee, O Lord our God, that we may soon behold the glory of Thy strength, that abominations may disappear from the earth and idols be entirely cut down, so that the world may be remedied through the Kingdom of the Almighty and all children of man may call upon Thy Name, and all the wicked of the earth may turn to Thee. All inhabitants of the world will perceive and know that to Thee every knee should bow and every tongue swear. Before Thee, O Lord our God, will they kneel and fall and to the glory of Thy Name will they grant honour and they will all accept the yoke of Thy Kingdom. And Thou shalt soon reign over them for ever and ever. For Thine is the Kingdom and for all eternity shalt Thou reign in glory.
uncertainties: 'abomina-tions' and 'King-dom' are line-break hyphens only.
'for ever and ever.' — the full stop looks slightly displaced (printed 'ever .'), possibly a spacing artifact.

blocks.text: אנסיכה I pay homage to my King, when I walk before Him, I praise His royal might, how He girds Himself with strength and reigns. When I cast away vanity, before the arrival of my king (the anointed) He will send the herald of my salvation (Elijah), and then will He reign. On his approach, falsehood will cease to reign, the house of the proud will not reign, it will be destroyed so that it can no more reign. He will walk in my midst, when he appears in order to reign, through his kingdom will I reign and then will He reign. The owners of kingdoms, when He shatters kingdoms, both nations and kingdoms will He confound and then reign. The scroll of the world’s paths, the book of the ways of life,

blocks.text: אהללה I praise my God, sing of His might, tell of His honour, I crown Him with a kingdom. I will exalt the Creator who spoke and created, I will glorify Him for the kingdom becomes Him. His might shall I ever repeat for I am of His host, and for me it is fitting to speak of the grandeur of the kingdom. In assembly do I proclaim, before a multitude of people do I announce whose is loftiness and might and whose is the kingdom. Approach, O nations, and come, O kingdoms, behold how glorious He is with the diadem of the kingdom. Call Him great with me, together let us exalt Him, do not behave proudly with the crown of the kingdom. When paths were laid through the depths of the sea, they all understood to whom was granted the kingdom. His horse walked through the sea against six hundred chariots of war, what did might avail man against the kingdom. Princes heard and then trembled, they looked around in dread and abdicated their kingdom. Peoples told of His power and said: to Him shall be written the name of the kingdom. The first people (Amalek)
